_spec: BANZA clean-room semantic closure — what every package must contain regardless of profile
_status: NON-NORMATIVE. This file records a CLASSIFICATION: which normative artifacts are required globally rather than by a profile. It points at the manifest; it defines no rule.
_why_this_exists: The L0 package was self-contained — every reference it included resolved — and contained no root trust plane at all, because the package is built from profile closures and those artifacts are correctly non-profile. 'Not scoped to a profile' had become 'not in any package'. Self-containment describes what is present; it says nothing about what is absent.

requirement_classes.GLOBAL: required by every implementation at every profile — an implementation cannot verify anything without it
requirement_classes.PROFILE: required by a specific conformance profile, and derived from the implementation sets
requirement_classes.CONFORMANCE: material for demonstrating conformance; expresses requirements defined elsewhere
requirement_classes.LEGAL: the legal basis for implementing at all
requirement_classes.INFORMATIVE: published and stable; imposes no obligation

global_required.why: who may exercise Root authority and how that changes — every trust evaluation starts here
the shape of an authority set
the succession vectors, carrying real signatures
ordering, rollback and equivocation across trust artifacts
BCJ/1 — the exact bytes that are signed and hashed; nothing in the trust plane works until this is exact
the invariants an implementation must not violate
what is normative, and what is not
the version in force and the compatibility rule
the vectors for the freshness, rollback and equivocation rules — the spec that defines them is globally required, so the material that validates an implementation of them is too

out_of_profile_pointers._why: A normative document may point at material that a given profile does not require. Silently tolerating those links is how the L0 gap happened, so each is declared here with the reason it is not included. A pointer NOT listed here is a closure failure, not a judgement call.

pointers.why: federation trust evaluation is an L3 concern; an L0 implementation does not route to a peer
the federation flow is out of scope below L3; the freshness rule itself is stated in full where it is defined
a pointer to the separately distributed conformance package, not a rule
